'''''Aeonium glandulosum''''' is a species of [[subshrub]] of the family [[Crassulaceae]] [[endemic]] to the [[Madeira|Madeira archipelago]] ([[Madeira Island]], [[Porto Santo Island]] and [[Desertas Islands]]).

==Description==
It is a biennial or perennial glandular-pubescent sub-shrub with a very short stem, hidden by the leaves, occasionally [[stolon]]iferous. It has [[Rosette (design)|rosette]]-shaped leaves, flat and plate-like but becomes centrally dome-shaped when the flowering season approaches, {{convert|30|cm|in}} in diameter. It has loose inflorescences, {{convert|30|x|45|cm|in}} with {{convert|3|-|19|mm|in}} pedicels that become distally curved. Petals are {{convert|7|-|10|mm|in}}, pale yellow and occasionally tinged with red.<ref name=uma>{{cite web |title=Aeonium glandulosum (Ait.) Webb et Berthel. |url=http://www3.uma.pt/biopolis/planta.php?id=177 |website=www3.uma.pt |access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The species is endemic to Madeira Island, Porto Santo Island, Desertas Islands and [[Bugio Island]] and is commonly found on sea cliffs in northern shores or rocky peaks from sea level up to {{convert|700|m|ft}} in altitude.<ref name=uma />
